findings.quote: at first halted, since the enemy held their pikes upright
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna: τὰς μὲν ἀρχὰς *** ἐπέστη, τῶν πολεμίων ὀρθὰς ἀνασχόντων τὰς σαρίσας. Text is missing after τὰς μὲν ἀρχὰς; the English reads on as if whole and supplies a causal 'since'.
findings.proposed_fix: at first [...] halted, the enemy having held their pikes upright

units.note: Rest checked: twenty σημαίας, left/right wings, Titus/vanguard all accurate.
Numbers 700 / 8000 / 5000 correct. Greek breaks off at τοιοῦτον (chapter ends mid-sentence in the source).

findings.quote: nor did he wish, having driven Philip from power, to leave the Aetolians as masters of the Greeks
findings.problem: Greek is εἴτ᾽ οὐκ ἐβούλετο ... : εἴτε is disjunctive ('or whether he did not wish'), the second member of an alternative of motives, not a negative continuation ('nor'). The first member lies in the lacuna.
findings.proposed_fix: or else he did not wish, having driven Philip from power, to leave the Aetolians as masters of the Greeks

units.note: Both lacunae are properly marked [...]. Context lost, so the exact first alternative cannot be restored.
Lacuna after δύ᾽ ὀνόματα is marked [...]. 6000 talents, 25 talents dowry, Scipio Aemilianus (natural son of Aemilius, adoptive grandson of Africanus) all correct.
Phaeneas' clause (μάταια πάντα τὰ πρὸ τοῦ γέγονε) is rendered 'would be in vain'; tense is loose but the sense is not inverted.
